name: Slate
short: Your own price book, and the estimate it builds in a minute.
long: Every rate the business charges lives in one book — labour, materials, plant, extras — with cost, markup and sell price side by side and editable in place. Building an estimate is typing a few words and picking lines out of that book; the total, the VAT and the deposit move as you go. The customer gets a real A4 document they can sign with a finger and pay the deposit on.
proves: The price you agreed on the doorstep and the price on the paperwork are the same price.
features: 47-item price book in four categories, edited in place, sell price computed from cost and markup
Estimate lines pulled from the book by typing, with optional sections the customer chooses later
Live total panel: VAT on or off, deposit at 0/10/25/50%, and what that deposit actually is
A true A4 preview on letterhead that prints as an A4 estimate and nothing else
Send, then the customer's own view: tick the optional extras, sign the box, pay the deposit
Rates are snapshotted onto an estimate when the line is added, so re-pricing the book never rewrites a sent quote
Everything survives a reload; Reset demo puts the book and the seven estimates back
story: Most small firms price a job twice — once in their head on the doorstep and again at the kitchen table at ten at night. This keeps the rates in one place and turns them into a document the customer can accept before they change their mind.
